schema.title: Response List Users Api V1 Admin Users Get

post.description:
Invite a user of one of the tenant's verified email domains, as ``invited``.

They then request a sign-in link from their own browser; the first sign-in makes
them ``active`` (findings A15). An email that exists in any tenant is refused:
Authentik's usernames are emails, and an email maps to one tenant (findings A8).

patch.description:
Change role or status. Deactivated users are refused at sign-in and on every
request; reactivating returns them to ``active``, or ``invited`` if they never
signed in.

put.description:
Default mode, model and reasoning of a new conversation in the workspace, among
the modes and models the operator enabled for the tenant (P1a-03, P1a-09).

post.description:
Tenant discovery (P1b-06): the methods the address's domain allows. Domain-level
only, so it says nothing about whether the address belongs to a user; an unknown
domain gets the links-only answer, like any domain without SSO.

Clear the session cookie and revoke the session server-side (P1a-02): the token
is listed in ``revoked_sessions``, so a copy of the old cookie is refused.

Start a sign-in through the address's tenant's source. An unknown domain and a
domain without SSO get the same 409: discovery already tells the page which.

schema.title: Response List Conversations Api V1 Conversations Get

post.description:
Start a conversation in a workspace with a mode, model and reasoning, all fixed.

Defaults come from the workspace; the mode is checked against the tenant's
``answer_modes``, the model and reasoning by ``choose_for_new_conversation``
(catalogue, ``enabled_models``, external-models entitlement, reasoning switch and
the external spend cap, P1a-09 to P1a-11). At the cap an external model falls back
to the workspace default and the response carries the notice.

delete.description: Hard delete: messages, citations and feedback go with it (ON DELETE CASCADE).

200.description: Server-Sent Events: any number of `token` events, then one `citations` event, then `done`; or `error` in place of the remainder. Each frame's `data` is the JSON object named after its event in ChatStreamEvents.

404.description: No such conversation for this user

get.description: Serve our stored copy of the file behind a single-use link of this user.

404.description: Unknown, expired or already used link

get.description: The signed-in user, from the request context (P1a-02).

post.description: Thumbs up/down on an assistant message in one of the user's own conversations.

get.description:
The models the tenant's users may pick (P1a-09): enabled for the tenant, and
external ones only with the external-models entitlement. ``default`` marks the
tenant-wide EU fallback; the start panel pre-fills from the workspace's defaults
(``GET /workspaces``).

Open or close the licence gate of one source, from its licence basis. Audited

schema.title: Response List Tenants Api V1 Operator Tenants Get

post.description:
Create the tenant's admin as ``invited`` and provision them in Authentik.

They then sign in with a link from their own browser; the first sign-in makes
them ``active``. An email already used in any tenant is refused: Authentik's
usernames are emails, and an email maps to one tenant (findings A8).

put.description:
Sign-in links on or off (on by default), JIT provisioning from the tenant's SSO
source, and the MFA requirement for tenant admins. Audited with before and after.

delete.description:
Remove the tenant's source from Authentik; its users then sign in with links (if
the policy allows them) until a source is configured again. Audited.

put.description:
Configure the tenant's one SSO source in Authentik and keep its non-secret fields.

The client secret (OIDC kinds) goes to Authentik only. A new source, or a change of
kind, needs it; otherwise omitting it keeps the one Authentik holds. Audited with
the kind, the source slug and a fingerprint of the stored configuration.
